slides.headline: THESE 5 AI PROMPTS DO THE $4,700 RECRUITER'S ENTIRE JOB FOR FREE
1) WRITE THE JOB DESCRIPTION THAT SCARES OFF TIME-WASTERS
slides.body: Recruiters charge $300+ to write a job description that actually filters for the right person. A generic posting pulls every applicant with a pulse. 📋 PROMPT: "Write a job description for [ROLE]. Include must-have skills that eliminate unqualified applicants, a task they will do on day one, and a screening question at the bottom that requires a specific answer to filter copy-paste applicants."

slides.headline: 2) SCREEN 100 APPLICATIONS IN 10 MINUTES
slides.body: Paying a recruiter to screen and shortlist runs $1,500 to $3,000 as a standalone service. AI reads the entire stack in one session and ranks the best by fit. 📋 PROMPT: "Here are [X] applications for [ROLE]. Rank every applicant by fit using these must-haves: [list your criteria]. Give me the top 5 with a one-sentence reason each, and flag red flags in the rest."

slides.headline: 3) BUILD INTERVIEW QUESTIONS CANDIDATES CAN'T REHEARSE
slides.body: A recruiter spends 2 to 3 hours building a tailored interview framework per role. Every generic list is already on Google and most candidates practice those answers the night before. 📋 PROMPT: "Write 5 interview questions for [ROLE] that require a real, specific example from the candidate's past, not a rehearsed story. For each question include the signal a strong answer must contain."

slides.headline: 4) SCORE EVERY CANDIDATE SO THE DECISION MAKES ITSELF
slides.body: A bad hire costs $15,000 on average in replacement, retraining, and lost output. Most bad hires come from gut-feel decisions made after a full day of back-to-back interviews. 📋 PROMPT: "Here are my interview notes for [CANDIDATE NAME]: [paste notes]. Score them 1, 10 on technical skill, culture fit, and communication. Give a hire or pass recommendation with one sentence of reasoning."

slides.headline: 5) WRITE A PROFESSIONAL OFFER LETTER IN 3 MINUTES
slides.body: Employment lawyers charge $200+ an hour to draft an offer letter. Most owners wait 48 hours for a callback and lose the candidate to a faster competitor in the gap. 📋 PROMPT: "Write a professional offer letter for [NAME] for the role of [ROLE] at [COMPANY]. Salary [X], start date [DATE]. Include job title, compensation, at-will employment language, and a 48-hour acceptance deadline."
